takeaway: Cerebral blood flow = cerebral perfusion pressure / cerebral vascular resistance (CPP/CVR). In an adult, typically 750 mL/min, 15% of the cardiac output.

lines.text: Here the equation is CPP over CVR.
lines.say: Here the equation is cerebral perfusion pressure over cerebral vascular resistance.

lines.text: CPP is the cerebral perfusion pressure,
lines.say: C P P is the cerebral perfusion pressure,

lines.text: and CVR is the cerebral vascular resistance.
lines.say: and C V R is the cerebral vascular resistance.

lines.text: Pressure divided by resistance gives a flow:
the cerebral blood flow, the blood supply per unit area of brain tissue per unit time.
In an adult it is typically 750 mL per minute, or 15 per cent of the cardiac output.
lines.say: In an adult it is typically seven hundred and fifty millilitres per minute, or fifteen per cent of the cardiac output.

lines.text: It is directly proportional to blood volume, but inversely related to CVR.
lines.say: It is directly proportional to blood volume, but inversely related to cerebral vascular resistance.
